dedupe_keys.name: landslides and road damage along the costa viola transport network calabria 1950 2025

description: This study maps landslides and road damage along the Costa Viola in south-western Calabria, where rain-induced landslides are among the most recurrent hazards to the transport network. Combining geomorphological mapping, multi-temporal analysis, historical documents (1950 to 2025) and GIS processing, the authors mapped 261 landslides covering about 19 percent of the area, mostly slides (66.7 percent). More than 80 percent occur in fractured granitic and gneissic rocks, over 70 percent within 500 m of faults and over 90 percent within 300 m of streams. The historical record holds 237 road damage events over 75 years, rising since the early 2000s, mostly on the SS18 road and often reactivations of older landslides in autumn and winter rain. Coverage: the Costa Viola coast. Format and access: open access article in GeoHazards (2026). Licence and cost: CC BY, free. Caveats: whether the inventory is released as data is not stated in the abstract. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of coastal roads. It relates to the European Ground Motion Service and the Czech railway tree fall case in the catalogue.
